title: contributor page — the public document of one person's published page
description:
The one public document of a contributor page (FS04-057's "public impact page", as ops decision D116 makes it customisable; design PROFILE-PAGE-2026-10-06 §4 and §8). `jobs.index-build`, the only writer of the public plane, writes it at `p/{pid}.json` from the person's newest published version of `contributor-page-settings.v1`, their current facts, the certificate records, the registry's names and their adopter facts, with every link rebuilt from `link-platforms.v1` and every colour checked. The website edge turns it into the HTML page on each request, with no script and no third-party request, at `https://purposesource.org/p/{pid}`, `/u/{login}` or `/u/{login}/{pid}`; the render job draws the card from it. It is written only while the page is published, and deleted when the person hides or deletes the page or their account (D116 item 10: hiding deletes the files); a hidden page answers exactly like one that never existed.

WHAT IT NEVER CARRIES (design §8.7). No points, shares, bands, ranks, percentiles, months or amounts: no member has such a name, and the sections are never ordered by any measure. The one exception is a certificate item's `months` (1.6.0), which names that certificate's own validity period as its public record already states it (`certificatesSection`), never a month of the monthly credit records (design §8.1). No `subId` and no other GitHub account id of the person (the plan's correction 11; design correction 5): the GitHub picture's source address names the numeric id, so it never enters this document either, and the picture travels only as our own re-encoded file. No draft: index-build has no read of drafts. No claim status: a repository is `registered` or `no-longer-registered`, never `verified` (D82 item 3). Facts are years only, a certificate's own period aside (above). No login the person did not choose to show: without `login`, no repository group is owned by the person's own account, because its owner's name is the login (`repositoriesSection`), and no GitHub Sponsors button names it (`contributor-page-settings.v1` check (b)). No date finer than a day: `generatedAt` is truncated to its UTC day, and `versionId` is random bits, never a ULID.

WHAT A READER CHECKS. It is a contributor's own page: Purpose Source checks the certificates and the repository facts on it, not the owner's words or links (the fixed footer, design §4.6). The about block (1.2.0) is Purpose Source's explanation of what the page's work means, or the owner's own words under their heading, followed by ours: not a fact Purpose Source checks. Each certificate row links to its verify page, where the signature is checked; each repository row links to its registry record; each adopter item links to the evidence on GitHub. Where this document and a certificate record or a registry record disagree, those records govern and the difference is a defect to report, so `x-psn.authoritative` is false. The footer's fixed "Report this page" opens the site's existing abuse form with the page's address in the fragment; reports reach legal@purposesource.org, are answered within five business days by the operator or a steward, a page is hidden first when in doubt, and a threat to life or safety is escalated at once (the D116 dated note of ~11:50Z, item 4). A steward's hide deletes this document like the person's own.

THE PREVIEW HASH (design §3.6). The person publishes exactly what they previewed: the private preview is this document as the builder would write it, and publishing sends its `previewSha256`, which the api recomputes from the current draft, facts, certificate displays, registry names and address, answering `409 page.preview_changed` with the new preview on a mismatch. `previewSha256` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the RFC 8785 (JCS) serialisation of the PREIMAGE, which is this document with exactly these changes: (1) the members `generatedAt` and `versionId` removed; (2) `card.h16` removed, where present; (3) a `picture` whose `kind` is `github` replaced by `{"kind":"github"}`; (4) from 1.5.0, the `picture` of every repository group and of every adopter item removed, where present (an organisation's picture, `$defs.organisationPicture`: the private preview names none, because the api copies nothing, and the published document gains each as its copy appears). Nothing else is removed or changed: `source`, `pid`, `factsAsOf`, `autoUpdated`, every section, the letters of a monogram and the `h16` of an uploaded picture or cover all stay, so an upload is pinned to the exact file the person previewed. Every string in the document is well-formed Unicode, with no lone surrogate (I-JSON, RFC 7493, which RFC 8785 assumes): the text rules refuse one at save (`contributor-page-settings.v1` `identity`), and a builder that met one would fail rather than serialise it, because JSON.stringify, UTF-8 encoders and System.Text.Json each write it differently. Every number in the document is an integer and every member name is ASCII, so JCS here is: members sorted by their UTF-16 code units, no whitespace, strings escaped as ECMAScript's JSON.stringify escapes them (non-ASCII characters are written as themselves, never as `\u` escapes). `examples/contributor-page-preview.v1.golden.json` holds worked vectors, and `check:contributor-page` recomputes them. After publishing, only what `autoUpdated` lists may change without a new preview.

FILES. Our own re-encoded files are named by `h16`, the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of a drawing's first file, and live beside the document under `p/{pid}/`: a picture as `a-{h16}-256.webp` (the page) and `a-{h16}-96.png` (the card); an uploaded cover as `c-{h16}-1600.webp` and `c-{h16}-800.webp`; the card as `card-{h16}.png`, `card-{h16}@2x.png`, `card-{h16}-dark.png`, `card-{h16}-dark@2x.png` and `og-{h16}.png`; from 1.5.0 an organisation's picture on its project and licence cards as `o-{h16}-96.png` (`$defs.organisationPicture`). The edge serves a file only while the live document names it. Every path is unlisted: counted in the publish log, never named. An uploaded picture or cover lives only as long as `contributor-page-settings.v1` `$defs.upload` says: its public copies leave with the document that named them, and hiding the page deletes the upload itself, so a page published again after a hide needs a new upload.

x-psn.phase: P-M3 (producer: `jobs.index-build`, slice P14g). Nothing is published under this contract yet: no page can be published before the api (P14d) and the editor (P14i) exist, and production publishes none until the published privacy notice describes the page and the operator turns `PSN_PAGE_PUBLISH` on (D116 item 10; slice P18).
x-psn.artifactPath: /p/{pid}.json in the public plane — unlisted (counted in /meta/publish-log.json, never named), read by the website edge only, rendered at https://purposesource.org/p/{pid}, /u/{login} and /u/{login}/{pid}; never served as JSON at a public route (/v1/p/{pid}/version answers its versionId)
x-psn.producer: `jobs.index-build` (P14g) through the one builder (`ContributorPageBuilder`, packages/Psn.Artifacts), which the api also calls for the private preview, so the preview is byte-equal to what is published. Until the person can publish, the private preview's document may hold no vouched section, or no section at all (`sections: []`, the default settings of an account with nothing credited and no certificate): anyone signed in may build and preview a page (the D116 dated note of ~11:50Z, item 1), the api answers such a preview with `preview.vouched` false and refuses to publish it, and only a published document must hold one, as `sections` says
consumers: the website edge renderer (`website/src/lib/contributor-page/`), for the page, the private preview and `?view=card`
the render job, which draws the card from it
the edge's `/v1/p/{pid}/version`, `/cards/p/…` and `/badge/p/…` routes, which answer only through the live document
fsRefs: FS04-057 (the public impact page, generated share-card image)
D116 items 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 10, and its dated notes of 2026-10-06 ~09:40Z and ~11:50Z
D149 items 1 to 4, 6 and 7, and its dated note of 2026-10-15
D163 items 1 to 5, and its dated notes of 2026-10-16

generatedAt.description: The plane's envelope instant (FS-00 §6.2), derived from the rows the build read — the version row among them — and TRUNCATED TO ITS UTC DAY, so it always ends `T00:00:00Z`. The document is readable at storage by anyone holding the pid, and the version row's instant to the second would date the person's publish more finely than the page itself ever does: the print footer already shows the day ("Page as published {date}"), and the fine print's "Repository names as listed in the registry on {date}" prints the same UTC date, so the day is accepted and nothing finer is published. The alias leaves its `generatedAt` out for the same reason. Rebuilt pages carry a new one when the day moves; unchanged bytes but for it are not rewritten. Left out of the preview hash.

source.description: Which plane produced the document, in the envelope's vocabulary (FS-00 §6.2): `platform` is `jobs.index-build` in `PSN_ENV=prod`, `fixture` every other environment, `sample` a sample plane. `sample` and `fixture` declare a non-production plane, which a production deployment refuses to serve (T5), answering the same 404 as for a page that never existed.

pid.description: The page's permanent id and its anonymous address `/p/{pid}`: 16 lower-case Crockford base32 characters of 80 random bits, not a ULID, so it dates nothing (design §2.3, §7.1). Printed in the footer and the QR. "Start over with a new permanent link" mints a new one, and the old answers like a page that never existed.

versionId.description: The published version this document was built from: `pgv_` and 26 lower-case Crockford base32 characters of 130 random bits, opaque to a reader. RANDOM, NEVER A ULID: the house mints certificate ids as ULIDs, whose first ten characters are a millisecond timestamp, and a ULID here would date each publish to the millisecond on a public route (`/v1/p/{pid}/version`) — design §2.3's reason for the pid. `/v1/p/{pid}/version` answers it, and the editor polls that route until it matches. Left out of the preview hash: it is assigned at publish.

address.description: The address the person chose (D116 item 2; design §7.1). The edge serves `/u/{login}` only when this is `login` and `login` matches, and `/u/{login}/{pid}` only when this is `mixed` and `login` matches; otherwise 404, never a redirect. `/p/{pid}` serves the page while this is `anonymous`; while it is `login` or `mixed`, a page view of `/p/{pid}` answers a temporary redirect (`302`, never `301` or `308`) to that address, and its card view is never redirected (ops decision D138). Where the edge cannot serve that address with this page, for example while its login alias (`contributor-page-alias.v1`) is not yet published or names another page, `/p/{pid}` keeps serving the page itself. The page's canonical link, `og:url` and that redirect name the chosen address; the edge builds every URL from its own origin, so this document names no host.

search.description: Whether search engines may list the page (D116 item 3). False sends `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` and the robots meta everywhere; true leaves both out on the `login` address only, never on `/p/{pid}`. True only with `address: login`.

login.description: The person's GitHub login, present only when they chose "Show my login" (status-only by default: the plan's item a and correction 11), and then shown in the header on a line of its own as "GitHub @login" with the "✓ Verified" chip, the only chip of its kind on the page (D116 dated note of ~09:40Z; ops decision D149, design CPAGE-REFINEMENTS-2026-10-15 §3): the chip always shows, and `loginShow` says which of the logo, "GitHub" and "@login" do. The current login: a rename is followed automatically, the old login address retired (`contributor-page-alias.v1`). The `login` and `mixed` addresses and the adopter section need it.

loginShow.description: As `contributor-page-settings.v1` `identity.loginShow` (1.1.0): which of the GitHub logo, the word "GitHub" and "@login" the GitHub line shows, at least one. The builder writes it only with `login`, and only when it is not all three.

theme.description: The preset and, where the person chose one, the accent the api adjusted (design §4.3). The renderer never adjusts: it checks each adjusted colour against its row's ground and surface in the theme table (`examples/contributor-page-contrast.v1.golden.json`) at 4.5:1 and, if one fails, falls back on that ground alone to the row's own accent (the print row's for print). Status chips always use fixed status tokens with an icon and words, so an accent cannot fake "Verified" or "Revoked". WITH A GROUND (1.1.0; ops decision D149 item 2): `ground` carries the rows the page is drawn on instead of the preset's own, and `accent` is always present, adjusted against them, so the renderer never has to choose one; its keys follow the rows: `raw`, `light` and `print`, and `dark` exactly when the ground has a `dark` row. The renderer checks each ground row as it checks the accent (ink and muted at least 4.5 against the row's ground and surface, the focus ring at least 3) and, where a row fails, draws the preset's own rows instead: its light row alone, or on `purpose` with a palette pair both of them, with the accent's `dark` (an own colour on `purpose` has no `dark`, so it falls back to the light row alone), and says so in its fallback.

accent.description: The accent as stored (`raw`, used only for decoration: the cover tint, the rules, the rosette) and as adjusted for each ground (links, headings, buttons): `light` for the page's own ground, `dark` for the dark ground of `purpose` (and only there), `print` for white. Without a `ground` it is present only where the person chose an accent. With a `ground` (1.1.0) it is always present: the builder runs the accent guard against the ground's rows (`light` and, for a `purpose` pair, `dark`) and the preset's print row, from the person's accent, or, where they chose none, from the preset's own accent for each row (on `purpose` its row of the same mode, otherwise its one row, and the print row's for print), with `raw` the colour the page's own row started from.

ground.description: The background the person chose (`contributor-page-settings.v1` `theme.ground`, 1.1.0; ops decision D149 item 2; design CPAGE-REFINEMENTS-2026-10-15 §5.6), as the rows the page is drawn on. `raw` is the settings' value as stored, a palette id or `#rrggbb`; `light` is the page's own row, whatever its mode (the convention of `accent.light`); `dark` is present only for a `purpose` palette pair, whose night row lets the page follow the visitor. A palette row keeps the preset's own ink, muted and focus ring; its surface is its ground mixed toward white by 32/64 on a light row and 4/64 on a dark one, and its rule the ground mixed toward the ink by 10/64. An own colour's row is the ground guard's (`contributor-page-settings.v1` `theme.ground`) and fixes the page's mode. Print keeps the preset's print row, on white. `examples/contributor-page-ground.v1.golden.json` holds every palette row and the guard's vectors.

raw.description: The settings' `theme.ground` as stored: a palette id, or an own colour `#rrggbb`.

light.description: The page's own row, whatever its mode.

dark.description: The night row of a `purpose` palette pair, and only there.

allOf.$comment: A dark row is a purpose pair's night: its day row is light, its raw is a palette id, never an own colour.
The accent's dark ground follows the rows: purpose's own dark row with no ground, or a ground's dark row (a purpose pair); never otherwise.
With a ground the accent is always present, so the renderer never chooses one.
Only purpose follows the visitor: a palette swatch of purpose is a day and night pair, and no other preset has a night row.

picture.description: The header's picture (design §6.3; the D116 dated note of ~11:50Z, item 2). `upload`: the person's own upload, at `p/{pid}/a-{h16}-256.webp` and `-96.png`. `github`: the person's GitHub picture as the render job copied and re-encoded it, at the same names once `h16` is present; until the copy exists the page draws the monogram from `letters`, or else the rosette, and the editor says the picture appears within a few minutes. `monogram`: `letters` on the accent. `rosette`: drawn from SHA-256("contributor-page:" + pid), decoration and never proof. Never a URL: no visitor's browser contacts GitHub or any other host.

letters.description: The monogram's one or two graphemes, computed by the builder (the first grapheme of the first and last words of the display name, or of the login where it is shown), so the renderer segments nothing.

cover.description: The cover (design §4.4), drawn only by the `profile` layout, as the banner the person chose; `paper` and `minimal` draw none (ops decision D149 item 6). An `upload` lives at `p/{pid}/c-{h16}-1600.webp` and `-800.webp`. No text ever sits on it.

identity.description: The header's words, as the settings hold them and index-build checked them again at this build; a member the person left empty is absent. Escaped at render; the bio keeps its line breaks and is never linked.

about.description: The about block (1.2.0; ops decision D163; design D163-ABOUT-TEXTS-2026-10-16), written only while the person's tick is on (`contributor-page-settings.v1` `about.on`): absent, the page has no about block, because the tick is off or the version was saved before 1.2.0. Drawn first, right under the header, before `sections`. It is not a section: never vouched (a page needs a vouched section in `sections` all the same), never on the card, never in `autoUpdated`, and the words it names never change on a published page, because `version` pins them; it is inside the preview hash like every member, so new words are a new preview. Its words are `contributor-page-about.v1`'s at `version`: for `short`, `medium` and `long` that variant's heading and paragraphs, then the proof sentence and the invite, which the renderer composes at every render from this document's own sections (the proof sentence names only what the page shows: listed valid or expired certificates, listed repositories or the summary's projects count, adopter items) and withholds the invite where certificates are not issued on the document's plane (production, `source` `platform`, until ops decision D160 item 8 opens them there, and a public sample, `source` `sample`, which every site build draws, production's included; `examples/contributor-page-about.v1.golden.json` `certificatesIssued` names each plane), ending then with a "Learn more" link; for `own`, that file's own heading, the person's `text`, our one line and "Learn more". A renderer that does not hold `version` leaves the block out rather than draw other words. Escaped at render; the person's text keeps its line breaks and is never linked.

variant.description: As `contributor-page-settings.v1` `about.variant`, as built: the settings' `own` with no words, or with words the text rules now refuse (the store's readers take such stored words as none, so the version is still built), is built as `short`.

version.description: The version of `contributor-page-about.v1` whose words the block shows: the settings' `about.version`, frozen with the published version.

text.description: The person's own words, exactly as the settings store them and the text rules accepted them again at this build: at most 600 code points and five line breaks. Only with `own`.

linksPlacement.description: As `contributor-page-settings.v1` `linksPlacement` (1.1.0); the builder writes it only when it is `header`. Then the links section, which keeps its shape and its place in `sections`, is drawn in the header after the bio, under the GitHub line, with no heading, and its place in the order is ignored; absent, it is drawn where `sections` puts it, headed "Elsewhere".

cards.description:
The settings' `cards` (1.3.0; ops decision D165), resolved: the one builder writes all three members on every document it builds, each the settings' choice or, where the settings leave it out, its default, so a published page keeps the choices it was previewed with even if a default later moves. A document built before 1.3.0 has no `cards`, and the renderer reads an absent `cards`, or an absent member, as its default (`icon` `owner`, `ownNames` `name`, `otherNames` `owner/name`), so it still draws. Inside the preview hash like every member; not a section, never on the card, never in `autoUpdated`.

HOW THE THREE LISTS ARE DRAWN (D165 items 1, 2 and 4). The credited projects (`repositoriesSection`), the licence adopter's repositories (`adopterSection`) and the certificates (`certificatesSection`) are never collapsed: each is a matrix of cards by default, in the document's order, with a quiet toggle beside its heading (a grid icon and a list icon, "Show as cards" and "Show as a list") that switches that section alone to a compact list. The toggle works without script, is reachable and visibly focused by keyboard, and the viewer's choice is never stored; nothing in this document chooses it. A repository is OWN when its owner is this document's `login`, compared without regard to case, and OTHER otherwise; a document without `login` lists no own repository (`repositoriesSection`), so every owner on it is OTHER. A project card shows its icon, its name by `ownNames` or `otherNames` (its group's `owner` and its row's `name`), its credited years where the row carries them ("Credited 2026", or "Credited 2026–2027"), "(no longer registered)" where its repository left the registry, and links to its registry record as the row does. A licence repository card shows its icon, its name by the same rule (the owner and the name of its `fullName`), its years where the item carries them (1.4.0: "Since 2026", or "2026–2027" for a repository that left the licence; `adopterSection`) and its evidence link on GitHub. A certificate card is a small certificate sheet: "Contributor certificate", the period large, its status line as `status` words it, the projects a `full` item names (by `fullName`, as its record names them), "Check this certificate" linking to its verify page, and its id in small type; it takes no icon and no name choice. The icons: `owner` draws, for an own repository, the picture `picture` names by a file (`github` with its `h16`, or `upload`), and nothing where it names none; for an OTHER owner, the organisation's own picture where its group or item names one (1.5.0, `$defs.organisationPicture`: only an organisation's, by GitHub's own answer for the repository, and never a person's), else a monogram tile, the owner's first letter in upper case on a colour picked from the owner's login (compared without regard to case, so one owner has one colour on the page) among the page's palette accents, its contrast checked as the page's other text; never a person's picture but the page owner's own, and nothing fetched from GitHub when the page is viewed. `github` draws the GitHub mark; `none`, nothing. Every fact, link, word and check of the three sections stands as each section says; only their presentation changes. The card choices are the page owner's presentation, not a fact Purpose Source checks.

ownNames.description: As `contributor-page-settings.v1` `cards.ownNames`: how a card names a repository whose owner is `login`.

otherNames.description: As `contributor-page-settings.v1` `cards.otherNames`: how a card names a repository of any other owner.

allOf.$comment: Design §2.2: a published page shows at least one vouched section. It is about contribution, not free link or fundraising hosting on our domain.

sections.description: The sections the person switched on and that have something to show, in the person's order, each at most once, below the fixed header and above the fixed footer. At least one is a vouched section (summary, certificates, repositories or adopter): the api refuses to publish otherwise, and index-build leaves the page as it was published rather than write one without.

card.description: What the card shows (design §4.9): each element already the AND of the person's switch and of the page showing it. `h16` names the card's files once the render job has drawn them and index-build has copied them; until then the card URLs answer the generic card. The card never carries a figure, a status or a QR.

h16.description: The card's files `card-{h16}.png`, `card-{h16}@2x.png`, `card-{h16}-dark.png`, `card-{h16}-dark@2x.png` and `og-{h16}.png`; the og image's URL carries `?v=` and its first eight characters. Left out of the preview hash: the card is drawn from the published document.

autoUpdated.description: What may change after publishing without a new preview (design §3.6), and the editor says so beside each switch ("Updated automatically after each month closes"): `summary`, the counts; `repositories`, the list in `all` mode; `adopter`, the adopter list; `certificate-status`, each certificate's status (from 1.7.0 with whether a superseded one's record names its successor, `successorNamed`); `registry-names`, repository and owner names; `login`, the login after a GitHub rename; `github-picture`, the GitHub picture where it is the chosen picture; `organisation-pictures` (1.5.0), the organisations' own pictures on the project and licence cards (`$defs.organisationPicture`), written from the settings alone while `cards.icon` is `owner` and the projects section, or the adopter section with the login shown, is switched on, so the preview hash never moves with what GitHub answers. Nothing else changes until the person publishes again.

factsAsOf.description: The last locked month whose credit records the facts include (design §8.1-§8.2): the summary's "updated" line. Null before any locked month has been read, as on production before the first monthly credit run. A month is the network's, the same for every page, so it dates nothing about a person.

allOf.$comment: Design §2.2 and §7.1: the login and mixed addresses carry the login.
Design §2.2 and §7.5: only the login address may be listed.
Design §2.2: a full record's verify page shows the login and would unmask a page without it; listing a status-only certificate on a named page would undo the person's own status-only choice.
Design §2.2 and §8.5: the adopter evidence names the login on GitHub.
1.1.0: the GitHub line's parts are written only on a page that shows the login.
1.5.0: the organisations' pictures are kept current only where the cards draw the owner's picture (an absent cards, or an absent icon, is owner).

h16.description: The first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of a drawing's first file (a picture's 256-pixel WebP, a cover's 1600-pixel WebP, a card's 1x light PNG, an organisation's picture's one 96-pixel PNG); the drawing's other files share it.

organisationPicture.description: 1.5.0 (ops decision D165 item 3, "the project's owner or organisation picture"; the orchestrator's CW-41 and its answer of 2026-10-18T09:25Z): an ORGANISATION's own GitHub picture, drawn on that owner's project and licence cards in place of the monogram tile, as our own copy `p/{pid}/o-{h16}-96.png`: fetched by the render job from GitHub's picture host alone (`org.avatar.requested`, the sibling of the owner's `page.avatar.requested`), its first frame cropped to the centre square and re-encoded to a 96-pixel PNG with no metadata, then copied beside the document by index-build. Never a URL, and never a person's picture. WHOSE: it is named on a group or item only where GitHub's own answer for EVERY repository this document shows under that login, in the projects and the licence adopter's sections together (the owner's `__typename`, stored with the owner's node id; never guessed from a login or an id), says the owner is an `Organization`, one and the same, under that very login (compared without regard to case); never on the page owner's own login, whose own repositories keep the page's own picture; and only while `cards.icon` is `owner`. So one login carries one `h16` on the whole page, and an answer that is missing, a `User`, or stale (a login that moved) leaves the tile. A repository owned by any other user keeps the tile: that is another person, who chose nothing here. Absent until the copy exists; outside the preview hash (its step (4)); kept current under `organisation-pictures` (`autoUpdated`): when the organisation changes its picture, the next publish asks for it again, and a new copy is a new `h16`.

show.description: As `contributor-page-settings.v1` `$defs.show` (1.1.0): the logo, the name and the handle ("@login" on the GitHub line), at least one.

websiteShow.description: As `contributor-page-settings.v1` `$defs.websiteShow` (1.1.0): the globe and the word "Website"; the domain always shows.

groundId.description: As `contributor-page-settings.v1` `$defs.groundId` (1.1.0): every palette id of `examples/contributor-page-ground.v1.golden.json`, once each.

groundRow.description: One row the page is drawn on (1.1.0): the theme table's tokens less the accent. `ground` is the page, `surface` the paper sheet and the profile cards, `ink` and `muted` text, `rule` a hairline (decoration, held to no figure), `focus` the focus ring. The status chips keep their fixed tokens of `mode`, and logos are pure black on a light row and pure white on a dark one, so neither depends on the person's colour.

years.description: Calendar years only, `from` no later than `to` — never months, shares or month counts (design §8.1: monthly detail would recreate a public trace of which months a person worked).

githubNodeId.description: A repository's GitHub node id, in the current `R_…` form or the legacy base64 form of "010:Repository…". Narrower than the house pattern `repo-record.v1` carries, which admits any object's id: this is the one document that must never carry the person's own id (the plan's correction 11), so a user's node id (`U_…`, or the legacy "04:User…") cannot pass where a repository id belongs.

fullName.description: `owner/name` as the registry lists it at this build, so renames follow.

summarySection.description: "Contribution" — "Credited on 7 projects in 3 organisations since 2026 · 2 certificates" (design §4.5, §8.1). Each count is present when the person switched it on and it is not zero; counts are over what the page's choices show, so a count never reveals a hidden repository, and on a page without `login` they leave out the repositories under the person's own account, as `repositoriesSection` does. The facts are locked monthly credit records (`micro_shares > 0` read only inside a function that answers years) and the person's own certificates; a year stays only while the monthly records hold it, or for good when a certificate covers it. A repository's years are credited years only (ops decision D137 item 4): the monthly records' wherever they answer for it; a valid, or clock-expired, participation certificate whose period lies in one calendar year adds that year to each of its projects; one whose period spans years (all-time, which runs to the newest locked month) adds its span only to a project nothing else answers for, so it never widens a repository's credited years. `since` is the earliest year of the repositories the page shows, never a listed certificate's own first year, and is absent when it shows none. `certificates` counts the certificates the page lists, except a revoked one whose credit never stood (see `certificatesSection`), which no total counts. Never titled "Impact" and never carrying an amount.

certificatesSection.description:
The person's own certificates the page lists, each with its type words, its period and live status chip — "Verified: attests participation in 2026", "Revoked", "Updated, see new", "Replaced" (1.7.0) — and "Check this certificate", linking to `/verify/{cid}`, where the signature is checked. On a page that shows the login every item is `full` and lists its projects, except a certificate revoked as `issuance-error` or `fraud-misrepresentation`, or revoked with no class or one the builder does not know (ops decision D137 item 4: its credit never stood, or nothing shows that it stood): that item is listed with its years and its "Revoked" chip and no `repos`, and is counted in no total; on a page that does not, every item is `status-only` and shows its type, years and status only (the plan's correction 9: certificates are status-only by default). Drawn as a matrix of certificate cards (1.3.0), never collapsed, each a small certificate sheet as `cards` describes.

THE PERIOD (1.6.0; the orchestrator's answer of 2026-10-21T20:26Z). An item names its period by its months (`months`), which the one builder writes on every item from 1.6.0; a reader of an item without them, built before, names it by its years, as before. The words, the same on the card and in the status chip: a whole calendar year reads "2026"; one month "February 2026"; months within one year "February–March 2026"; months across years "November 2026–January 2027". A period is always whole locked months, a whole year or all-time, so no form names a day, and only the months tell a month's certificate from its year's. The verify page's verdict on a contributor's certificate names its period in the same words, from the record's own `period`.

THE SUCCESSOR (1.7.0; the orchestrator's decision of 2026-10-27 on the CW-47 B follow-up). A `superseded` item says whether its record names the certificate that replaced it (`successorNamed`), which the one builder writes on every superseded item from 1.7.0. Where the record names one, the chip reads "Updated, see new", and "see new" opens the item's own verify page (`/verify/{cid}`), which links that certificate. Where it names none, the chip reads "Replaced", in the same neutral tone, with no link: since platform `c38d22f7` a superseded record leaves `supersededBy` out when the certificate that replaced it, or a later one in its line, was withdrawn by its holder or has no public record of its own, and its verify page then names no successor and links nothing, as its badge says `replaced` (`badge.v1` 1.4.0). A reader of a superseded item without `successorNamed`, built before 1.7.0, draws "Updated, see new", as before. The page never carries the successor's id: a reader finds it in the record, and only where the record names it.

typ.description: A person's own certificates are contributor certificates (FS08-010); a later type is an additive widening.

years.description: The years of the certificate's validity period, as its record states them.

months.description: 1.6.0 (the orchestrator's answer of 2026-10-21T20:26Z): the certificate's validity period by its months, each `YYYY-MM`: `from` the month of its record's `period.validFrom`, `to` the month of its `period.validUntil` (`certificate-record.v1`), `from` no later than `to`, and each in the year `years` names on its side (check:contributor-page holds the order and the years, which a schema cannot). Every public record states that period, a status-only one included, so the page names nothing its verify page does not. The one builder writes it on every item from 1.6.0; an item without it, built before, is drawn by its years. Only here: `years`, `$defs.years` and every other fact stay years only, never a month of the monthly credit records (design §8.1).

status.description: The record's status at this build (`certificate-status` in `autoUpdated`). A participation certificate `expired` only by the clock still reads "Verified: attests participation in {period}" (`certificatesSection`, THE PERIOD); a `superseded` one reads "Updated, see new", or "Replaced" where `successorNamed` is false (`certificatesSection`, THE SUCCESSOR); print shows no chip.

successorNamed.description: 1.7.0 (the orchestrator's decision of 2026-10-27 on the CW-47 B follow-up): on a `superseded` item only (the schema refuses it beside any other status), whether the item's public record (`certs/{cid}.json`, `certificate-record.v1`) names the certificate that replaced it: true where the record carries `supersededBy`, a certificate id; false where it carries none (the member left out, or null, as the verify page reads it). The one builder writes it on every superseded item from 1.7.0, right after `status`, by the same reading of the certificate's line of successors that decides the record's `supersededBy` (platform `c38d22f7`: none where that line leaves the published records or reaches a certificate its holder withdrew), so the page never promises a successor its verify page does not name. It moves with the status (`certificate-status` in `autoUpdated`). False draws the chip "Replaced", with no link; true, or an item without it (built before 1.7.0), draws "Updated, see new" (`certificatesSection`, THE SUCCESSOR). A boolean, never an id: the page names no successor itself.

disclosure.description: The record's own disclosure (`certificate-record.v1` `disclosure`), which this page must match.

repos.description: A `full` item's projects, by their registry names at this build. Never on a `status-only` item, whose record drops its scope, nor on a revoked item whose credit never stood (`certificatesSection`).

repositoriesSection.description: "Projects" — the credited repositories the person chose, grouped by owner, groups and rows in name order and never by contribution size (design §4.5, §8.1). Each row links to `/registry/repo/{nodeId}`; with the person's `years` switch on, every row carries its years and reads "Credited 2026–2027", and with it off none does; the years are credited years only, as `summarySection` says. ON A PAGE WITHOUT `login`, NO GROUP IS THE PERSON'S OWN ACCOUNT: a repository whose owner is the person's GitHub login (the current one, compared without regard to case) would print that login in plain text as its group's name, the very disclosure the person declined by leaving "Show my login" off (the plan's item a and correction 11; the reason design §2.2 refuses GitHub Sponsors under the person's own login). The one builder therefore leaves such repositories out of this section and out of the summary's counts, at the preview and at every build, and the api refuses one the person selects by hand (`page.repository_shows_login`, `contributor-page-settings.v1` check (j)). This document cannot show the rule, because the login it compares with is exactly what the document leaves out; `examples/contributor-page-build.v1.golden.json` holds the builder's vectors for it, and `check:contributor-page` runs them. Drawn as a matrix of project cards (1.3.0), never collapsed, each named and given its icon by `cards`. A group whose owner is an organisation carries that organisation's own picture for its cards (1.5.0, `picture`, `$defs.organisationPicture`).

owner.description: The owner's login, already public beside every registry row.

listing.description: Never `verified`: that internal state means claimed, and D82 item 3 keeps claim status from anyone but the admins. "(no longer registered)" is printed beside a row whose repository left the registry.

picture.description: 1.5.0: the owner's own picture, on a group whose owner is an organisation (`$defs.organisationPicture`); absent on every other group, which draws the monogram tile.

adopterSection.description:
"Licence adopter" — "Merged the Purpose Source License into N repositories" (D116 item 7; design §8.5): registered repositories, and from 1.4.0 those that have left the licence since (below), where this person merged the adoption pull request (`merged-pr`) or committed the licence text themselves (`direct-commit`), read from GitHub with the person's own authorisation. GitHub already publishes both facts; the page puts them side by side by the person's choice. It reads no claim data. Each item links to its registry record and to the evidence, rebuilt by the renderer as `https://github.com/{fullName}/pull/{number}` or `…/commit/{oid}`. Drawn as a matrix of repository cards (1.3.0), never collapsed, each named and given its icon by `cards`; an item whose repository's owner is an organisation carries that organisation's own picture for its card (1.5.0, `picture`, `$defs.organisationPicture`).

SINCE AND UNTIL (1.4.0; ops decision D168 item 3, the operator's "since which year each repo is adopted or since - until in case the repo is no more under the license but it used to be"). `since` is the UTC calendar year of the item's own evidence on GitHub: the merge of its pull request (`merged-pr`), or its commit's committed date (`direct-commit`). A 1.4.0 builder writes it on every item whose evidence date is stored; an item without it (a fact stored before its date was, which the person's next check dates) shows no year, never a guessed one. LEFT means a quit (FS-02 T5): the repository's LICENSE changed away from the Purpose Source License, its text removed or replaced, as the licence watcher finds it (FS02-042's `quit` and `quit-file-deleted`) and the registry records it, so it is no longer under the licence. A left repository stays listed with `until`, the UTC year of the registry's recorded quit event, and only with both years, `since` no later than `until`; no other item carries `until`, which would say that a repository left the licence when it did not. Nothing else is a leave: an item whose repository was delisted (T7, for cause) or suspended (gone, blocked, archived or private), or quit with no recorded date (a repository imported from registry-v0), or quit before its evidence, or left with no evidence date stored, drops out of the section as before 1.4.0, so a page never shows a repository that left as though it were still under the licence; and a repository of the Association's own is never listed, left or not (ops decision D167). A repository registered again (T8's restore) carries `since` alone. The renderer draws "Since 2026" in the card's quiet row and at the end of the list row (ops decision D166), "2026–2027" for a left item (one year where both are the same), and nothing for an item without `since`. Years only (design §8.1): no instant leaves the platform.

since.description: 1.4.0: the UTC year of the item's own evidence, its pull request's merge (`merged-pr`) or its commit's committed date (`direct-commit`), as GitHub records it. Written wherever that date is stored; absent, the item shows no year.

until.description: 1.4.0: on a LEFT item alone (the section's description), the UTC year of the registry's recorded quit event. Only beside `since`, and never earlier than it: check:contributor-page holds the order, which a schema cannot.

picture.description: 1.5.0: the owner's own picture, on an item whose repository's owner (the first half of `fullName`) is an organisation (`$defs.organisationPicture`); absent on every other item, which draws the monogram tile.

linksSection.description: "Elsewhere" (design §5.2, §5.4; ops decision D149, design CPAGE-REFINEMENTS-2026-10-15 §1, §2): the social links, rebuilt from `link-platforms.v1` at this build, and the one personal website. Each link is drawn with its platform's real logo, in plain black or white and never the accent, and with the parts its `show` names (absent: the logo, the platform's name and the handle); links that show only their logo stand side by side as plain logos, never in boxes; a part not shown stays in the link as hidden text, so its accessible name is always the platform and the handle. Every platform link carries `rel="nofollow ugc noopener noreferrer"` (plus `me` for Mastodon) and no `target`: it goes to the platform's own domain and opens directly. The website, the one link that may name any domain, opens the edge's heads-up page (ops decision D178 item 4), the address the page is served at followed by `/leave`, in a new tab (`target="_blank"`, `rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer"`); that page shows the domain and the whole address before the reader goes on, and the page's head names the website itself in `<link rel="me">`. With the document's `linksPlacement: header` the section is drawn in the header after the bio, under the GitHub line, with no heading. Only the GitHub line carries the "✓ Verified" chip, and the fixed footer says Purpose Source checks the certificates and the repository facts on the page, not the owner's words or links; no other line about the links is drawn. THE RENDERER DRAWS A LINK ONLY WHEN IT REBUILDS THE SAME ADDRESS: from the item's `{platform, form, handle, instance}` it checks the handle against the form's grammar (an absent `form` being the platform's first), judges it (the table's step 6), finds a Mastodon `instance` on the table's list, and rebuilds the address (step 7: the template filled in, the output rule asserted), and draws the item only when the result equals `url`, character for character; otherwise it leaves the item out. So the visible text, which names the handle, and the `href` can never name two different accounts. The handle's character class is checked here too, per platform as `contributor-page-settings.v1` `$defs.link` checks it, so no bidi control or other stray character reaches the link text even before the renderer runs.

handle.description: The handle as the table's steps left it, its character class checked per platform below (the same coarse classes as `contributor-page-settings.v1` `$defs.link`); the table's grammar decides the rest, and the renderer rebuilds `url` from it.

show.description: As the settings' `links[].show`; written only when it is not all three (1.1.0).

website.description: The one personal website, with its full host shown (the renderer decides the Unicode or `xn--` form, `link-platforms.v1` `website.displayScripts`). `show` (1.1.0; absent: both) says whether our globe and the word "Website" show beside it; the domain always does.

sponsorsSection.description: "Support {name} directly" (design §5.3): our own buttons, "Support on {platform}", each with its sponsorship platform's real logo in the button's text colour, or its words alone where no logo is confirmed (ops decision D149 item 7), no amount, goal or count, and the fixed line, marked for counsel: "These links go to other services. Purpose Source takes no part in these payments. They are not Purpose Fees or donations to the listed charities." Each button is drawn only when the renderer, rebuilding the address from `{platform, form, handle}` as for a link (`linksSection`), gets exactly `url`.

linkUrl.description: An address rebuilt from `link-platforms.v1`: its form's template with the handle substituted, on the host the template fixes (strict output). No input reaches it except through the handle's grammar.

socialPlatform.description: The `social` platforms of `link-platforms.v1`; `check:links` asserts this copy equals the table.

sponsorPlatform.description: The eight `sponsorship` platforms of `link-platforms.v1`; `check:links` asserts this copy equals the table.
